flag.truss: Span {width} m > 30 m — roof switched automatically to a 2L angle truss ({chord} chords, {diag} diagonals).
flag.portal: Span {width} m ≤ 30 m — solid-web {raf} rafter with haunched moment connections.
flag.doorShrunk: Door size reduced to {w} × {h} m to fit the building.

notes.0: Bay spacing is distributed evenly along the building length. Wind columns are placed on the gables at most 5 m apart; those falling in the door opening are replaced by door posts.
notes.1: Girts run on all four walls: on side walls they bolt to the columns, on gables to corner columns, wind columns and door posts through a 20 mm cleat plate with 2 × M12. Gable girts shorten with the roof slope and are cut at the door opening.
notes.2: Knee and apex joints are haunched moment connections with extended end plates. At truss nodes a 20 mm gusset plate sits between the 2L legs.

flag.thick: {floors} storeys: raft thickness 50 cm + {extra} cm = {total} cm.
flag.min: {floors} storeys: minimum raft thickness of 50 cm applied.

notes.0: Column spacing is distributed evenly across width and length and never exceeds the selected maximum. Raft thickness is 50 cm up to 3 storeys, then +10 cm per additional storey.
notes.1: Primary beams in the strong-axis direction connect to the column flange with end plates (moment); weak-axis primary beams and secondary beams connect to the web with fin plates (pinned). Columns are spliced with end plates every 3 storeys.

spec.roofScrew: self-drilling for sheet / steel, with seal
spec.cleat: at every purlin / girt – frame intersection

flag.lowSlope: Below 5% pitch, trapezoidal sheeting needs additional sealing measures.

notes.0: Sheet counts are based on a 1000 mm cover width, a 200 mm end lap and a 5% waste allowance; they are nominal values. The wall area includes the gable triangles.
notes.1: The grey translucent main frame is for display only (not in the take-off). Purlins and girts connect to the frame through a 20 mm cleat plate with 2 × M12 bolts.

flag.load: {name} load class ({q} kN/m²) — preliminary sizing: {col} columns, {main} primary beams, {sec} secondary beams.

notes.0: When the load class changes, column and beam profiles are suggested automatically for preliminary sizing; you may change them from the catalog. The final profile selection requires a structural calculation by a licensed engineer.
notes.1: Primary beams connect to the column cap with an end plate; secondary beams connect to the primary beam web with a fin plate. Stair stringers bolt to the edge beam through an end plate at the top and to the ground through a base plate at the bottom.

flag.gates: Length is not enough for {wanted} gates; {placed} gate(s) placed.

notes.0: Embedment depth is added to the post length. Gates are spaced evenly along the length; gate openings are deducted from the rail and infill take-off. Unit weights come from the profile catalogue; the paint surface is computed from the profile perimeter (AL).

flag.doors: Wall length is not enough for {doors} doors; {placed} placed.

notes.0: Waste and consumable factors are average site values; door openings are deducted. Door jambs have double studs and a head track (UW).
notes.1: The drywall frame consists of light galvanised profiles joined with screws; no steel connection plates are used. See the "Profile catalogue" button for all steel profile series.
